title: START YOUR DAY WITH THIS POWERFUL PSALM 120 PRAYER — DON'T LEAVE HOME WITHOUT IT
text: Stop whatever you are doing. I don't care if you are in the middle of making breakfast. I don't care if you are in your car one foot already out the door. I don't care if this is coming through your earphones while you are rushing to get ready. Stop. Just stop for this moment because what I am about to share with you is not content, it is covering. And there is a difference between content you consume and covering you carry. You can consume content and go home the same. But when covering comes on you, the atmosphere around you changes. The trajectory of your day bends and the forces that were waiting to ambush your morning find out that you did not leave home unprotected. >> [music] >> I am going to talk to you about something this morning that is so practical, so immediate, so urgent that I I almost cannot begin without first dealing with the culture we have developed as believers. The culture of rushing out into the day without spiritual preparation. We eat before we leave. We check our phones before we leave. Some of us spend more time picking an outfit than we spend in the presence of God and then we wonder why the day feels like a battlefield we entered unarmed. The prophet Isaiah said in Isaiah chapter 50 verse 4, "The Lord God had given me the tongue of the learned that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary. >> [music] >> He wakened morning by morning. He wakened my ear to hear as the learned. Morning by morning. Not when you finally get around to it. Not at lunch time. Not in the evening when the damage has already been done. Morning by morning." And so this is your morning, whether it is literally morning when you are receiving this or whether this is the morning of a new season in your life. This is your word in season. Receive it with the ears of the learned. Let us pray before we go in. Father, in the name of Jesus, I thank you for this gathering. I thank you for the hunger that drove this person to seek your presence before they stepped into the demands of the day. Lord, I ask that you honor that hunger. Meet them right here. >> [music] >> Let this not be another message they forget in 30 minutes. Let this be a word that goes so deep into their spirit that it changes how they begin every morning for the rest of their life. In Jesus' name, amen. Now, turn with me to the book of Psalms, chapter 120, verse 1. And then, we will also draw from Psalm 121, verses 1 and 2. Because these two Psalms form a continuum. They are sequential songs of ascent. Songs that the people of God sang as they journeyed upward towards Jerusalem, upward towards the presence of God. And together, they carry a revelation that will transform how you start every single day. Psalm 120, verse 1. In my distress, I cried unto the Lord and he heard me. That is the entire text. One verse. Seven words in the King James that carry the weight of an entire theology of morning prayer. In my distress, I cried unto the Lord and he heard me. Now, let me show you Psalm 121, verses 1 and 2. I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the Lord which made heaven and earth. Two Psalms, two postures, one reality. The reality is this, there is a God who hears, and there is a God who helps. And he's the same God, and his name is Lord. And before you leave home today, you need to access him. But let me take you deeper into Psalm 120, because there is so much that most people miss when they read this passage. This Psalm is one of 15 Psalms, Psalms 120 through 134, all titled a song of ascents or a song of degrees. And the Hebrew scholars have understood these Psalms in two significant ways. First, they were sung by pilgrims who were literally climbing the hill towards Jerusalem for the three great feasts, Passover, Pentecost, and Tabernacles. Every year, families would make that journey. Every year, they would walk upward, and as they walked, they sang these songs. These were journey songs, walking songs, ascending songs. But there is a second interpretation that these were the songs sung by the Levitical choir as they ascended the 15 steps of the temple. 15 steps, 15 songs, one per step. And each song was a progression, not just geographically, but spiritually. Each step represented a deeper level of ascent into the presence of God. And Psalm 120 is the first [music] song, the beginning of the ascent. And do you know where Psalm 120 begins? It begins in distress. Not in triumph, not in victory, not with shouts of hallelujah and banners waving. It begins in my [music] distress. And I want you to notice that the psalmist does not hide the distress. He does not sanitize his [music] entry into prayer. He does not pretend that everything is fine in order to approach God. He brings the distress [music] with him. He enters the ascent with the very thing that is troubling him. And beloved, this is your permission tonight or this morning, or whatever time you are receiving this, this is your permission to bring what you actually have, not the polished version of yourself. Not the version that has it all together. Bring the distress, bring the unresolved thing, bring the confusion, bring the fear, bring the lack, bring the broken relationship, bring the diagnosis, bring the question that has not been answered. Bring it all and begin to cry onto the Lord. Because the second half of that verse is the most important part, and he heard me. He heard me, past tense, already settled. The moment the cry went up, the hearing happened. There was no delay in the hearing. There was no let me check your record first. There was no I need to evaluate whether you qualify for my attention. The cry went up and the hearing happened. Now, somebody will say, "But if God heard me, why has the answer not come?" And that is a valid question that deserves a prophetic answer. The hearing and the manifested answer are not always simultaneous, but the hearing is always immediate. And the answer, though it may take time to materialize in the physical realm, is dispatched the moment the cry is heard. Daniel chapter 10:12, the angel said to Daniel, "Fear not, Daniel, for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words. From the first day, the hearing was first day, the arrival of the answer was 21 days later. But first day hearing, that is the promise, that is the covenant. That is what Psalm 120:1 is telling you about the nature of the God you are praying to. So, when you cry, he hears, and when he hears, he moves, and when he moves, nothing can stop the answer from arriving. Now, I want to show you something in the context of Psalm 120 that will set the stage for our morning prayer. >> [music] >> Look at verse two. Deliver my soul, oh Lord, from lying lips and from a deceitful tongue. The psalmist, after establishing that God hears, immediately brings a specific petition. And his first petition is protection from lying lips and a deceitful tongue. Why would this be the first petition of someone ascending toward God? Because the enemy's primary weapon is deception. The enemy cannot create anything, he can only corrupt. He cannot build, he can only destroy. And his most effective tool is the spoken word lies that are spoken over your life, lies that are spoken into your atmosphere, lies that you begin to believe about your situation, about God, about yourself. John 8:44, Jesus said of the devil, "He was a murderer from the beginning and abode not in the truth because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own, for he is a liar and the father of it, the father of lies. Every lie about your health from the father of lies, every lie about your marriage from the father of lies, every lie about your destiny from the father of lies. Every lie that says God has forgotten you from the father of lies, every lie that says your best days are behind you from the father of lies. And the psalmist understood something, before you go out into the day, you need to be delivered from the lies that have been spoken over your life. Because if you go out carrying a lie, you will make decisions based on a false reality. You will respond to life based on a narrative that was constructed by the enemy and not by God. This is why Psalm 120 has to be your morning prayer. It is a prayer of purification, a prayer of deliverance from false narratives, a prayer that establishes truth as the foundation before you step out of the door. And then look at verse 7. I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war. The psalmist is surrounded by people who are hostile. He's living in a context where his desire for peace is met with aggression. He wants peace. His environment is producing conflict. He's speaking reconciliation. Those around him are escalating war. Does that sound like anybody's daily life? You go to work trying to do the right thing and there are people in that office who are working against you. You are trying to maintain peace in your marriage and there is a spirit that is constantly stirring contention. You are trying to do business with integrity and there are forces trying to sabotage every deal. You are for peace, but your circumstances are for war. This is your morning reality and Psalm 120 is saying before you enter that reality, you need to have already prayed. You need to have already cried to the Lord. You need to have already been heard. Because the God who heard you in your prayer closet will follow you into the office. The God who heard you in your bedroom will walk with you into the boardroom. The God who heard you before you left home will be present in every environment you enter today. Psalm 121 picks it up. Verses 7 and 8. The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil. He shall preserve thy soul. The Lord shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth and even forevermore. Your going out, your coming in from this time forth. From this time forth. Not from some distant future time, from this time forth. Meaning from this morning, from this prayer, from this cry, divine preservation begins. Before you even get to where you are going, the Lord has already gone ahead to prepare the path. Let me preach this to you for a moment. In Exodus chapter 23 verses 20 and 23, God said to the children of Israel before they enter the promised land, "Behold, I send an angel before thee to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have [music] prepared. I send an angel before thee." The angel goes in advance. Before you arrive at that meeting, the angel has already been there. Before you step into that hospital appointment, the angel has already gone in ahead. Before you arrive at that office that feels hostile, the angel has already walked through it. But notice the condition in verse 21. >> [music] >> "Beware of him and obey his voice. Provoke him not for he will not pardon your transgressions for my name is in him." There is a condition of alignment. The angel operates in the context of your alignment with God. [music] And your morning prayer is what establishes that alignment. Your morning cry is what activates the angel. Your morning ascent, your Psalm 120 moment, is what releases the divine escort for your day. And so I am saying to you with every drop of apostolic urgency I have, do not leave home without this prayer. Not as a ritual, not as a religious habit, as a strategy, as a weapon, as a daily act of spiritual intelligence. Proverbs 27:12, "A prudent man foreseeth the evil and hideth himself, but the simple pass on and are punished." The prudent person sees the evil coming and hides before it arrives. Morning prayer is your spiritual foresight. It is you in the spirit seeing what the day carries before the day unfolds and positioning yourself in God before you step into it. Let me show you one more thing before we go into prayer, and this is the thing that will shift everything. In Luke chapter 21 verse 36, Jesus said, "Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of Man." Pray always that you may be accounted worthy to escape, not survive, not barely make it through. Escape. Escape the things that were assigned against you. Escape the traps, escape the accidents, escape the sickness, escape the financial devastation, escape the relational damage. The word escape here in the Greek is ekpheugo. It means to flee out from, to get out from under, to not be caught in. God wants you to not be caught in the things the enemy has set for this day. And the mechanism of escape is prayer. So, let us pray. And let us pray with the full weight of everything we have received from the word this morning. Father, in the name of Jesus, we begin this day. We begin this morning. We begin this prayer with the same words the psalmist began with. We are in distress. Not because we have no faith, but because we are honest. And because we know that the God who inhabits honest crying is greater than the God of polished presentations. >> [music] >> Lord, some of us are in distress about our finances. Some of us left the house this morning, or we'll leave in a few minutes with a financial situation that is wearing us down. The bills are not matching the income. The month is longer than the money. The promises have not yet manifested. And Lord, we are bringing this distress to you because you told us to cast all our care upon you, for you care for us. 1 Peter chapter 5 verse 7. Some of us are in distress about our health. There is a symptom that will not go away. There is a report that has been hanging over our head. There is a body that has not been cooperating with the life we're trying to live. And Lord, we bring that to you before we step out today. Some of us are in distress about a child. A child who is making decisions that are breaking our heart. A child who has walked away from everything we raised them to be. >> [music] >> A child who is in danger spiritually, physically, emotionally, and we do not know how to reach them. Lord, we bring that distress to you. Some of us are in distress about our purpose. We know we are made for more, but we cannot find the door. We have the hunger, but not the platform. We have the gift, but not the opportunity. And the delay is becoming a weight. Lord, we bring it. Receive every act of bringing right now. Receive every surrendering of care. Receive every honest cry from every person connected to this gathering. >> [music] >> Lord, receive it and respond to it the same way you responded to the psalmist. Hear us. Hear us, God. Let the hearing happen right now, and let the angels be dispatched. Let the processes be initiated. Let the breakthrough be activated even before this prayer ends. In the name of Jesus, we cry to you. Lord, we cry. We cry. Hear our cry. Now, let us go into warfare. I want to deal first with what the psalmist called lying lips and a deceitful tongue. Because before we pray about finances, before we pray about health, before we pray about family, we need to deal with the lies. Because lies are the infrastructure on which the enemy builds every other assignment. There are lies that have been spoken over your life. I want you to hear this carefully. Not just things that are factually untrue, but spiritual lies, prophetic lies, destiny lies. Lies that were declared at satanic altars specifically about your future. Lies that were spoken by people in your family who had no idea they were being used by the enemy. Lies that were spoken by people who were supposed to build you, but instead cost you. Lies that have been playing in your own thought life as though they were truth. The enemy does not fight fairly. He does not just attack your circumstances, he attacks your perception. He attacks the narrative. Because if he can control what you believe about yourself and about God, he does not need to control your circumstances. You will do his work for him by making decisions based on his lies. Romans 12:2, "And be not conformed to this world, but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God." Transformation begins with the renewing of the mind, >> [music] >> not the renewing of circumstances, the renewing of the mind. And morning prayer is the daily renewing of the mind. Let us pray with authority. Father, in the name of Jesus, we come against every lying spirit that has been operating in our atmosphere, every lying voice that has been giving us a false report about our future. Every spirit of discouragement [music] that has been whispering, "It will never happen for you." Every spirit of fear that has been projecting doom over our days. Every voice of the enemy that sounds like reason, but is actually deception. We silence you now in the name of Jesus. We break [music] the power of every false prophetic word that was spoken over our lives by people who spoke from a wrong spirit. If someone declared defeat over us, we cancel that word by the blood of Jesus. If someone said we would not amount to anything, we cancel that declaration in Jesus name. If a satanic altar was used to speak words of limitation over our destiny, let that word be destroyed right now by the fire of the Holy Ghost. Every evil decree against our morning scatter. >> [music] >> Every lie that was prepared to ambush us today be exposed in the name of Jesus. We declare no weapon formed against us shall prosper and every tongue that rises against us in judgment, we condemn it. Isaiah 54:17, we condemn the lying tongue. We condemn the deceitful report. We condemn the false narrative. We replace every lie with the truth of the word of God. The truth is I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Psalm 139:14. The truth is I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. Philippians 4:13. The truth is the Lord is my shepherd and I shall not want. Psalm 23:1. The truth is greater is he that is in me than he that is in the world. 1 John 4:4. The truth is I am more than a conqueror through him that loved me. Romans 8:37. The truth is the plans God has for me are plans of peace and not of evil to give me an expected end. Jeremiah 29:11. These are not affirmations. These are covenant declarations. They are backed by the blood and the word of the living God and they supersede every lie the enemy has planted. Receive that now. Let the truth go deep. Let it displace every lie. Let it uproot every false narrative and let truth be the atmosphere you carry out of your house today. Now we are going to pray about today specifically. Because Psalm 120 is not a general Psalm. It is a day specific cry. This is someone about to go somewhere, about to enter something, about to face the day, and they are covering the day before it unfolds. So, let us cover today. Father, in the name of Jesus, over this day. Lord, we cover this day with the blood of Jesus. We cover every appointment, every meeting, every journey, every transaction, every conversation, every decision that will be made today with the blood of Jesus Christ. Let no evil befall us this day. Psalm 91:10, "There shall no evil befall thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling." We stand on that covenant. No evil, no plague, no accident, no sudden disaster, no unforeseen collapse. God has promised, and God cannot lie. Lord, cover our vehicles today. Cover every road we will travel, every flight, every bus, every train. Lord, let [music] your angels cover the journey. Let there be divine navigation. Let what was supposed to go wrong today go right because of the blood of Jesus. Cover our workplaces today. There are principalities assigned to certain office environments. There are territorial spirits that operate in certain marketplaces. And Lord, we do not go into those environments unprotected. We go covered. We go shielded. We go with the name of Jesus as our banner. Proverbs 18:10, "The name of the Lord is a strong tower. The righteous runneth into it and is safe." We run into that tower right now. We position ourselves inside the name of the Lord before we walk into the challenges of the day, and we declare what is inside the tower is safe. My peace is safe. My mind is safe. My health is safe. My joy is safe. My destiny is safe. In Jesus' name. Lord, cover every appointment today. Every meeting that has a spiritual dimension to it that we cannot fully see, cover it. If there is a person in that meeting who has come with hidden agendas, expose the agenda before damage is done. If there is a decision that seems right to us but is actually a trap, Lord, close that door before we walk into it. Give us wisdom. Give us discernment. Give us the spirit of counsel. Isaiah 11 verse 2. I want to pray specifically now about the workplace and the marketplace. There are people going to work today in environments that are hostile to their faith. Environments where they are the only believer. Environments where the culture is corrupt. Environments where they have been overlooked, underpaid, disrespected, or overlooked for promotion in spite of their excellence. And they go every day carrying the weight of that injustice. Father, in the name of Jesus, we speak to every unjust situation in the workplace. Lord, you are the God of justice. Psalm 89 verse 14 says, "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne. And the same God whose throne is founded on justice will not allow injustice to permanently prevail against his children." Lord, let the favor of God be released over our work today. >> [music] >> Psalm 5 verse 12. "For thou, Lord, will bless the righteous. With favor will thou compass him as with a shield. With favor as a shield." Not just a blessing, a shield of favor. Meaning the favor of God will actually protect us from the things that attack us in the workplace. Let every supervisor who has been hostile receive a supernatural softening today. Let every door that has been closed to promotion or opportunity be opened today. Let the works of our hands be blessed. Let what we put our hand to prosper. Psalm 1:3, "And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water that bringeth forth his fruit in his season. His leaf also shall not wither, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper. Whatsoever he doeth shall prosper." That is the righteousness of the person who delights in the word of God. And that person is you, the person who began this day with the word of God. The tree by the river, the fruitful tree, the tree whose [music] leaf does not wither, the tree that prospers in whatsoever it does. I decree over your work today, prosperity. Not just financial prosperity of results, prosperity of relationships, prosperity of influence, prosperity of impact. Whatever you touch today will bear fruit. Whatever you build today will stand. Whatever you say today will carry weight. Whatever meeting you walk into today, you will leave an impression that only the anointing of God can explain. Now, let us go into an area of prayer that is very urgent, and that is the protection of our minds this morning. One of the most dangerous things you can allow to happen as you begin your day >> [music] >> is to leave without taking captive the thoughts that will challenge you. 2 Corinthians 10:5, "Casting down imaginations and every high thing that exalted itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ." Casting down imaginations. The word imaginations here in the Greek is logismos. It speaks of arguments, of reasonings, of elaborate mental constructs. The enemy does not just attack you with fear, he builds arguments. He builds logical sounding cases against your future. He presents evidence, your past failures, your current circumstances, your limitations, your age, your resources or lack thereof, and he constructs an argument for why things will not work out for you. And if you do not know how to cast down those arguments, you will spend your entire day losing a battle in your mind before you even get to the actual challenge. This is why Philippians 4:6 and 7 is one of the most strategic passages in the New Testament for daily living. Be careful for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication with Thanksgiving, let your request be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. Shall keep. The word for keep is phroureo. It is a military term. It means to garrison, to station soldiers around. The peace of God shall garrison your heart and mind. Soldiers stationed at the gates of your mind. No unauthorized thought gets through. No fear, no anxiety, no torment, no confusion, no doubt not pass the garrison of God's peace. That garrison is activated through prayer and supplication with Thanksgiving, and that is what we are doing right now. We are activating the garrison Father, in the name of Jesus, we speak to our minds this morning. We cast down every imagination that does not align with the knowledge of God. We cast down every anxious thought. Every worst-case scenario that fear has been projecting, every rehearsed failure, every anticipated rejection, every dreaded conversation, every anticipated disappointment, >> [music] >> we bring these thoughts into captivity right now. We do not give them the right to run free in our minds today. We submit them to the obedience of Christ and we replace them with the peace of God that passes understanding. Guard our minds today, Lord. Let no panic get past the garrison. Let no torment get past the garrison. Let no confusion, no depression, no suicidal thought, no self-destructive reasoning, let none of it get past what you have stationed at the gates of our minds. Let our minds be clear today. Let our thoughts be sharp. Let our decisions be wise. Let our words be seasoned with grace and power. Let our minds operate today under the anointing of the Holy Ghost, not under the pressure of the enemy. I decree no mental warfare shall prevail against you this day. No attack on your mind shall succeed. The peace of God is your garrison. The mind of Christ is your inheritance. 1 Corinthians 2:16, "For who hath known the mind of the Lord that he may instruct him, but we have the mind of Christ." You have the mind of Christ. Not a confused mind. Not an anxious mind. Not a defeated mind. The mind of Christ, a mind that sees from God's perspective, things with God's wisdom, and responds with God's grace. Shout amen if you receive that. Now, let us pray about what I want to call the hidden dangers of the day. There are things that will try to happen to you today that you do not know about. Hidden dangers, set traps, things the enemy has been arranging in the background. And Psalm 91 covers this comprehensively. Psalm 91:3-6, "Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence. He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shall thou trust. His truth shall be thy shield and buckler. Thou shall not be afraid for the terror by night, nor for the arrow that flyeth by day, nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness, nor for the destruction that wasted at noonday. The arrow that flies by day, destruction at noonday. This speak of dangers that come at you in full daylight, things that happen in the middle of your ordinary day, not the midnight attacks, the daytime attacks. The accident on the road during rush hour, the sudden health emergency in the middle of your work day, the unexpected collapse of a business deal at the last minute, the out of nowhere conflict that derails the day. Father, in the name of Jesus, we cover against every arrow that flies by day, every daytime danger, every ambush that has been set for our ordinary hours. We activate the covenant of Psalm 91 over our lives and the lives of our families right now. Lord, deliver us from the snare of the fowler. The snare is hidden, the snare is deceptive, the snare looks like an innocent path until your foot is in it. Deliver us from every snare that has been disguised as an opportunity, every trap that has been disguised as a relationship, every pit that has been disguised as a shortcut. Deliver us from the fowler's snare in the name of Jesus. Cover us with your feathers. That image is so tender, the image of a hen gathering her chicks under her wings [music] when danger approaches. Lord, that is what we are asking for this morning. Gather us under your wings before we step out. Cover us on every side, >> [music] >> above us, below us, on our left and on our right, before us and behind us. Let the covering of Almighty God be our reality today. And let his truth be our shield and buckler. Truth as a shield, the word of God as our defensive weapon. Let every lie that the enemy fires at us today hits the shield of truth and fall harmless to the ground. Let every false accusation, every slanderous word, every attack on our reputation hit the shield of truth >> [music] >> because what God has declared about us is the truth that overrules every human verdict. I want to go into a specific prayer for families right now because when we leave home, we are not just leaving to face our own battles, we are leaving behind the people we love to face theirs. >> [music] >> And one of the most powerful things a parent can do, one of the most powerful things a spouse can do, one of the most powerful things a family member can do is to pray for spiritual covering over the family before they part ways for the day. Deuteronomy 6:6-7 and these words which I commanded this day shall be in thine heart and thou shall teach them diligently unto thy children and shall talk of them when thou sittest in thine house and when thou walkest by the way and when thou liest down and when thou risest up. When thou risest up, when you rise up in the morning, the word of God should be the language of your household, not the news, not social media debates, not worry about the day's logistics as the first spiritual diet of the morning, the word of God. When thou risest up, let us pray for families. Father, in the name of Jesus, we cover our children today. Every child, biological, adopted, spiritual, who belongs to this gathering, Lord, cover them as they leave home for school, for work, for wherever the day takes them. Let your angels be assigned to them specifically. Let them walk in divine protection today. Cover them from wrong associations, from peer pressure that could lead them into destruction, from the wrong friend who could draw them into a path they were not designed for. Lord, give our children discernment at the level of their age and understanding. Let them know something is wrong before the trap closes. Give them the courage to walk away. Cover them from accidents on the road, accidents in the school environment, accidents in any environment. Lord, not one hair on the head of our children shall be touched by the enemy today. Luke 21:18, "But there shall not an hair of your head perish." That is the covenant we stand on for our children. For spouses, Lord, cover the marriages in this gathering as the family separate for the work of the day. Cover them from the temptations that come in the workplace. Cover them from emotional entanglements with people who are not their spouse. Cover them from the spirit of comparison and dissatisfaction. Cover the covenant. Cover the commitment. Let the love that was planted in that marriage by God be sustained and deepened even in the business of the day. For aging parents, for sick relatives, for family members who are in spiritually dangerous places, Lord, let your hand of protection be on them today. Let the angels watch over them. Let them experience the mercy of God in specific ways today. In Jesus' name. For prodigal children, children who have left the faith, who are in dangerous environments, who are in relationships that are destroying them, Father, let this be the day that something interrupts their trajectory. Let this be the day that the Holy Spirit arrests their attention. Let this be the day that the consequences of their choices become so clear to them that they make the turn. And Lord, let there be someone in their path today who carries the fragrance of God, someone whose word, whose example, whose kindness becomes the catalyst for for return. Luke 15:20 and he arose and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him and had compassion and ran and fell on his neck and kissed him. The father saw him when he was yet a great way off. Which means the father was watching. The father was positioned at the place of return even before the son arrived. Lord, position yourself at the place of return for every prodigal in our families. When they make the turn, receive them, embrace them, kiss them, let them know they are not too far gone and it is not too late. I decree the prodigal is coming home. The prodigal is coming home in the name of Jesus. Now, let me pray for something that I feel very strongly impressed by the spirit of God to address and that is the spirit that operates specifically in the morning to prevent you from praying. You may have never thought about this as a targeted strategy of the enemy but it is. There are specific demonic assignments that activate in the morning hours to prevent you from having your morning altar. Suddenly, you oversleep. Suddenly, there is a crisis that consumes your time before you have prayed. Suddenly, the children need something urgent. Suddenly, an email comes that takes your attention. Suddenly, there is an argument that disturbs your spirit before you get a chance to settle it in prayer and you end up leaving the house unprotected not because you wanted to, not because you don't know better, but because the enemy strategically used the morning chaos to shut down your prayer. Lamentations 3:23, they are new every morning. Great is thy faithfulness. The mercies of God are new every morning. There is a fresh supply of grace waiting for you at the altar every morning. >> [music] >> And the enemy knows that if he can get you to skip the altar, you go into the day without that fresh supply. Mark 1:35, "And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out and departed into a solitary place and there prayed." He, Jesus. "Rising up a great while before day," he woke before the demands could find him. He went out to a solitary place before the needs of the crowd could claim his morning and there he prayed.
